title: Southgate Clinic - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Southgate Clinic onboarding to Redwood. Covered goals, timeline for a 6-week pilot, security requirements (SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS), staging vs production networking (VPC), and next steps: share onboarding & security pack, schedule architecture deep dive, customer to share sample data schema.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-29
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood CSM), Dr. Samir Khan (CTO, Southgate), Janelle Ortiz (Head of Data), Ben Torres (InfoSec)
Shared: onboarding deck (link), security pack (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood. Quick roll call and then we'll run through the agenda. Lina is here for CS, Ethan's our solutions engineer.
[00:22] Dr. Samir Khan: Hi all, Samir here, thanks. Janelle and Ben from Southgate. Appreciate the time.
[00:35] Maya Patel: Great. Quick objective: align on pilot scope and timeline, get an architecture workshop scheduled, and surface any security or networking blockers up front.
[01:05] Janelle Ortiz: We're aiming to put a triage assistant into production for clinical intake forms, initial pilot for about 6 weeks, want to validate latency and answer quality. Also need clarity on PHI handling and retention.
[01:32] Ethan Ruiz: Awesome, thanks. For the pilot we usually recommend staging -> pilot prod flow. We'll propose a config using Redwood hosted API first, then Dedicated or Private if you need VPC/on-prem for PHI.
[02:05] Ben Torres: Quick note from InfoSec: we require SOC 2 evidence, SSO via SAML, audit logs, and options for KMS-managed keys. Also need network controls — can you support customer-managed VPC peering or private links?
[02:40] Ethan Ruiz: Yes. We support both VPC peering and private connectivity; our Private offering includes a customer-controlled VPC and an on-prem package if needed. For KMS we integrate with major providers — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSMs.
[03:12] Maya Patel: I'll send the security pack after the call which includes SOC 2 summary, pen test notes, and our KMS integration guide.
[03:30] Dr. Samir Khan: Great. One thing: cost — our finance team will want estimates for hosted vs dedicated. Can you give us back-of-envelope numbers for our expected throughput?
[03:58] Lina Gomez: We'll run a quick cost model — if you can give us expected qps and token size we can recommend batching and quantization settings. For pilot we usually target small instance so costs are manageable.
[04:25] Janelle Ortiz: Expected load is about 2k requests/day, average prompt ~120 tokens, peak concurrency maybe 5-10. Latency target is sub-500ms 95th for the triage flow.
[04:49] Ethan Ruiz: 500ms 95th is feasible on optimized models with small context and prefix caching. We'll likely recommend a mid-size open model or Redwood-optimized variant; we can do a smoke benchmark in staging.
[05:20] Ben Torres: How does caching work with PHI? We don't want to cache any PHI in persistent caches.
[05:36] Ethan Ruiz: Good question. We support configurable KV cache policies and can disable persistent prefix caching; ephemeral cache in-memory only, or turn off KV cache entirely. We'll document recommended settings for PHI workloads.
[06:05] Janelle Ortiz: Also, what about redaction/PII detection? Any built-in tooling?
[06:18] Ethan Ruiz: We have prebuilt redaction plugins and recommend a two-step pipeline — client-side redaction + server-side policies. We'll share the redaction checklist in the security pack.
[06:45] Maya Patel: Ok next on timeline: propose a 6-week pilot. Week 0–1 onboarding and staging setup, week 2–4 integration and iterating, week 5–6 evaluate metrics and decide on Dedicated or Private. Does that align?
[07:08] Dr. Samir Khan: That sounds right. We need legal sign-off on DPA and a vendor risk assessment — I'll loop in procurement.
[07:30] Ben Torres: Procurement will want the SOC2 and encryption lifecycle docs.
[07:38] Maya Patel: Understood — those are in the security pack. We'll also provide contract templates and a sample DPA.
[08:02] Janelle Ortiz: On integrations: we use an on-prem EHR with HL7 exports, and some patient intake forms in our web portal. We'll probably feed structured JSON to Redwood.
[08:22] Ethan Ruiz: Structured JSON is ideal. If you have HL7 feeds we can transform them into compact prompts. We'll want a sample schema.
[08:45] Janelle Ortiz: I'll add that to the shared drive after the call.
[09:00] Ethan Ruiz: For staging keys — we'll provision a sandbox project and ephemeral API keys so you can test without touching prod. That includes token-level cost analytics.
[09:20] Lina Gomez: From CS perspective I'll set up the success criteria doc — accuracy thresholds, latency, and false-positive/negative tolerances for triage categories.
[09:40] Dr. Samir Khan: Who will own monitoring? We need alerts if latency spikes or if there's a regression in answer quality.
[09:55] Ethan Ruiz: Redwood Console has per-route latency and token cost breakdowns and you can hook alerting to our tracing. We'll help wire that into your PagerDuty or Slack.
[10:20] Ben Torres: Do you offer long-term retention controls for logs? We need at-rest logs for 6 months with restricted access.
[10:35] Maya Patel: Yes, retention is configurable, and access is RBAC controlled. We'll include recommended retention settings in the security pack.
[10:55] Janelle Ortiz: Any blockers we've missed?
[11:05] Dr. Samir Khan: One more: model explanations / auditability. We need to be able to trace why the assistant made a classification — show prompt + model scores.
[11:22] Ethan Ruiz: We can export request/response traces and token-level logits for internal audits under a secured bucket. We'll redact PHI per your policy.
[11:40] Maya Patel: Ok let's talk pilot acceptance criteria — Lina?
[11:48] Lina Gomez: Proposed: 1) 95th percentile latency < 500ms, 2) triage accuracy > 88% on holdout set, 3) stable throughput for peak windows, 4) no critical security findings from vendor assessment. We'll draft and share.
[12:15] Janelle Ortiz: That seems fair. We'll add business KPIs like reduced manual triage time by X%.
[12:30] Ethan Ruiz: Implementation notes: we'll start with hosted API and do a quick benchmark on your sample data; if performance/cost tradeoffs require Dedicated we'll scope GPU sizing. For on-prem, procurement and security timelines typically add extra lead time.
[12:58] Dr. Samir Khan: Timeline for legal and procurement — expect 2–3 weeks for vendor review. Can Redwood provide a checklist for procurement?
[13:12] Maya Patel: Yes, procurement checklist included in pack.
[13:30] Janelle Ortiz: Are there any limits on model length or concurrent requests in staging?
[13:42] Ethan Ruiz: Staging has soft limits; we'll set them to mirror pilot quotas. For long contexts we recommend our streaming responses with prefix pruning to keep latency down.
[14:05] Ben Torres: Encryption in transit and at rest? Are keys customer-managed?
[14:16] Ethan Ruiz: TLS in transit, SSE for at-rest with options for customer-managed KMS. We'll include the KMS integration guide.
[14:40] Maya Patel: Quick recap of artifacts we'll send: onboarding deck, security pack (SOC2, KMS, redaction checklist), sample DPA, procurement checklist, and a staging access link.
[15:05] Dr. Samir Khan: Perfect. Any concerns about scaling from pilot to 100k requests/day?
[15:20] Ethan Ruiz: We have autoscaling policies and Dedicated pools. We'll do capacity planning after pilot — recommend a stress test in week 4.
[15:45] Janelle Ortiz: For the stress test we can simulate HL7 bursts.
[16:00] Ethan Ruiz: Good. We'll send a benchmark template to feed your traffic profile.
[16:18] Maya Patel: Alright final wrap — action items and owners noted. Lina will share success criteria doc, I'll send packs and contract samples, Ethan will schedule the architecture workshop, Janelle and Ben will share schema and procurement asks.
[16:40] Dr. Samir Khan: Thanks — we'll aim to have the schema and procurement contact by next week.
[16:52] Ben Torres: I'll check SOC2 details with procurement and send feedback.
[17:05] Maya Patel: Great. Next meeting: architecture deep-dive tentatively 2027-08-03 — Ethan will follow up with invite.
[17:20] Janelle Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
[17:25] Maya Patel: Thanks, bye.

Notes about transcript quality: general ASR noise around technical acronyms (HL7 sometimes transcribed as H-L-7, KV cache as kay-vee cache), occasional speaker overlaps, some proper nouns slightly off.

End of meeting.
